headline: Your APPROVE waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing equipment sellers into the right APPROVE offer. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for Josh Nielsen.
productSummary: APPROVE is embedded equipment financing for equipment sellers: a custom-branded finance program at every point of sale, a 60-second application, and instant match of each buyer to a lender network so they see up to 3 competing offers. Built by KWIPPED, it is aimed at equipment manufacturers, distributors, and dealers who want more approvals across the credit spectrum. Homepage proof: 82% of equipment buyers are looking for financing (Equipment Leasing & Finance Association, 2025). Also offers working capital and SBA for buyers. Companion marketplace: KWIPPED.
coreInsight: Brielle already pitched Josh on integrating financing into manufacturer and distributor buyer journeys. Amelia's earlier thread offered a 5-page cold-email and list-building doc. The one list is in-TAM equipment sellers LinkedIn and dealer directories already surface. The one routing signal is how financing currently shows up on their site, because a homepage scrape returns competitor widgets, a financing-available mention with no apply flow, a catalog with zero financing language, or none of those, in one pull. Industry labels are merge tags after the account is routed. They are not a second waterfall.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is how financing already shows up on their site
sections.takeaway: A dealer homepage already names a competitor widget, a financing mention with no apply button, a catalog with zero financing language, or none of those. That page-state is stronger than a title guess, and it is free to collect.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: One cascade routes every equipment seller
sections.takeaway: First match wins. Competitor finance widgets go first, then financing mentioned with no embedded apply, then a live catalog with no financing language, then every remaining in-TAM seller.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Each page-state gets a different first offer
sections.takeaway: Competitor widget gets a Lender-Competition Switch Brief. Financing-mentioned-but-not-embedded gets a POS Embed Brief. Catalog-with-no-financing gets an 82% Capture Brief. The rest get the Seller Finance Playbook.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: Switch the single lender, embed the apply, put payments on the catalog, then cover the rest
sections.takeaway: The list is always in-TAM equipment manufacturers, distributors, and dealers, aimed at owners, GMs, and VPs of Sales. Industry is a merge tag, not a second TAM. A/Bs sit on the exclusive routes.

sections.label: Email Copy
sections.title: Copy that names the financing state already on their site
sections.takeaway: Notice the widget, the phrase, or the missing payments line, poke the approval or drop-off gap that page-state implies, then ask for a one-letter yes.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Launch the competitor-widget route first
sections.takeaway: Start where they already believe in offering financing and are paying a single-lender partner. Prove reply density, then roll the embed gap, the silent catalog, and the remaining-TAM catch-all.

signalReasons: LinkedIn plus equipment-dealer directories are the TAM Brielle already named: manufacturers and distributors (plus dealers) who sell equipment and can embed financing at the point of sale.

The same site scrape returns a competitor widget (TimePayment, Navitas TurboTools/Bo, Ascentium, DLL, Leaf, Balboa), a financing mention with no apply flow, or a catalog with zero financing language, which is enough to route without a second enrichment product.
The ladder maps to live APPROVE positioning: competing lenders, more approvals across the credit spectrum, a 60-second application, and the ELFA 82% figure already on their homepage.
Industry labels are scrape filters and merge tags. They are not a second waterfall. Apollo is email last, never the TAM spine.

sources.name: LinkedIn Sales Navigator company + title graph
sources.delivers: In-TAM equipment manufacturers, distributors, and dealers plus owner / GM / VP Sales titles. The TAM gate.

sources.name: Homepage and product-page scrape
sources.delivers: finance_page_state used to assign Tier 1 / 2 / 3 / catch-all: competitor widget, financing mention, catalog with no financing, or none. One pull.

sources.name: BuiltWith / script and footer scan
sources.delivers: Named competitor widgets (TimePayment, Navitas Bo/TurboTools, Ascentium, DLL, Leaf, Balboa, Channel) when the scrape needs a second pass

sources.name: AED / industry dealer directories (optional)
sources.delivers: Backup in_tam when LinkedIn coverage is thin. Gate only.

sources.name: Apollo (after qualification)
sources.delivers: Work emails for already-routed accounts. Do not buy a raw CFO-at-manufacturers list and hope.

sources.name: Optional APPROVE / KWIPPED customer suppress
sources.delivers: Current-customer exclusion when the signal is visible. Thin coverage. Treat as a suppress list, not a tier.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND finance_page_state = competitor_widget (TimePayment, Navitas, Ascentium, DLL, Leaf, Balboa, Channel, or named single-lender partner on site)
routingRules.why: They already sell with financing and are locked to one lender. Strongest intent for competing offers and higher approval rates.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND finance_page_state = mention_no_embed (financing / leasing / monthly payments mentioned, no apply widget or branded program)
routingRules.why: They already believe financing closes deals, but the buyer still has to ask. Pain is drop-off, not education.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND finance_page_state = catalog_no_financing (product catalog, shop, or quote flow live, zero financing language)
routingRules.why: Buyers are shopping equipment with no payment path. Maps to the 82% ELFA figure on approvepayments.com.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND none of the above
routingRules.why: Still in TAM (equipment manufacturers, distributors, dealers). Softest CTA, broadest copy, mandatory 100% coverage.

tiers.name: Tier 1
tiers.label: Competitor finance widget on site
tiers.trigger: Homepage or product page shows TimePayment, Navitas, Ascentium, DLL, Leaf, Balboa, Channel, or another named single-lender partner
tiers.pain: They already offer financing but one lender caps approvals. Deals that would clear a competing network die in that one box.
tiers.valueProp: Show up to 3 competing offers from a lender network so more buyers get approved across the credit spectrum.
tiers.replyDensity: Highest - they already pay to offer financing
tiers.accounts: est. flagged; not published on approvepayments.com

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: Financing mentioned, not embedded
tiers.trigger: Site says financing / leasing / monthly payments available, but there is no apply widget, QR, or branded program
tiers.pain: The sales team still has to ask about financing, so deals stall while a buyer waits on paperwork.
tiers.valueProp: Embed a 60-second application into quotes, product pages, and emails so the apply happens at the point of decision.
tiers.replyDensity: High - they already named financing as a closer

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: Catalog live, no financing language
tiers.trigger: Product catalog, shop, or quote flow is live and the site never mentions financing, leasing, or monthly payments
tiers.pain: Buyers who need payments (82% per ELFA, cited on their homepage) bounce because there is no path.
tiers.valueProp: Put affordable monthly payment options on every product page and quote so those buyers can say yes.
tiers.replyDensity: Medium - catalog proves they sell equipment, urgency varies

tiers.name: Catch-all
tiers.label: Remaining in-TAM equipment sellers
tiers.trigger: In-TAM manufacturer, distributor, or dealer with a sales decision maker and no Tier 1-3 page-state
tiers.pain: Equipment deals still close as cash or stall without a branded finance program at the point of sale.
tiers.valueProp: A simple path to a custom-branded finance program without rebuilding the sales stack.
tiers.dataSource: LinkedIn company + title graph after in_tam gate
tiers.accounts: est. flagged; catch-all must cover remaining TAM

campaigns.name: Single lender already on the site
campaigns.strategy: Lead with the named {{competitor}} widget on their site, then offer a one-page Lender-Competition Switch Brief showing how peers put up to 3 competing offers in front of the same buyer.
campaigns.value: More approvals than one lender can clear

campaigns.name: They say financing, buyers still have to ask
campaigns.strategy: Name the {{finance_phrase}} on their site, poke the drop-off of asking about financing, offer the POS Embed Brief.
campaigns.value: Apply at the quote, not after it
campaigns.overview: Second exclusive route. Keep copy about friction, not education.

campaigns.name: Catalog with no payment path
campaigns.strategy: Lead with the live catalog and the missing payments line, then the 82% ELFA figure already on approvepayments.com.
campaigns.overview: Third exclusive route. {{industry}} is a merge tag.

campaigns.name: Remaining equipment sellers
campaigns.strategy: Soft Seller Finance Playbook. Industry and title as merge tags. Soft CTA.
campaigns.value: Simple path to a branded finance program

messages.subject: {{competitor}} on {{company_name}}
messages.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

Saw {{competitor}} on your site. Usually that means financing is live, but every buyer still has to clear one lender's box.

We put together a one-page Lender-Competition Switch Brief for {{industry}} dealers: how peers show up to 3 competing offers so more applications actually approve.

Worth a look?

Hey {{first_name}},

Quick bump on the Switch Brief. Happy to send the one-pager if {{competitor}} is still the only path on the site.

Either way, appreciate you.

messages.subject: question for {{first_name}}
messages.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

Should I close the loop on this, or is approval rate still something {{company_name}} wants cleaner than a single-lender widget?

A / B / C is fine.

messages.subject: financing on {{company_name}}
messages.body:

Your site already says {{finance_phrase}}. Teams in that spot usually still wait on the buyer to ask, so the quote dies in follow-up.

Happy to share a short POS Embed Brief: 60-second apply on the product page and in the quote, not after.

Useful?

Hey {{first_name}},

Just floating the POS Embed Brief again in case quote drop-off is a live topic this month.

No stress either way.

messages.subject: {{first_name}} / embed
messages.body:

messages.subject: payments on the {{company_name}} catalog
messages.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

Your catalog is live and I could not find a financing path on it. ELFA's 2025 figure (the one APPROVE cites) is that 82% of equipment buyers are looking for financing.

We sketched an 82% Capture Brief around putting monthly payments on every product page.

Want it?

Hey {{first_name}},

Bump in case the catalog is still cash-only this quarter.

Happy to send the brief or drop it.

messages.subject: close the loop?
messages.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

Keep / send / stop - whatever is easiest.

Thanks either way.

messages.subject: finance program for {{company_name}}
messages.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

For {{industry}} sellers, the usual drag is quotes that only work if the buyer can pay cash.

Put together a short Seller Finance Playbook: how peers add a branded program at the point of sale without rebuilding the stack.

Open to a look?

Hey {{first_name}},

Floating the playbook once more in case financing at the quote is on the list this month.

messages.subject: ok to close?
messages.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

Fine to close this out if timing is off.

A yes / no is plenty.

launchPlan: Confirm in_tam definition: equipment manufacturers, distributors, and dealers who sell B2B equipment and can embed financing at POS (APPROVE seller product on approvepayments.com).
Pull Sales Nav for those companies, then scrape homepages for finance_page_state. Suppress known APPROVE/KWIPPED customers.
Launch Tier 1 only until reply density is clear (target ~1 positive / 150-300).
Add Tier 2 mention-no-embed once Tier 1 copy is stable.
Add Tier 3 catalog-with-no-financing, then the catch-all for remaining in-TAM sellers.
Enrich emails via Apollo only after the account is routed.
A/B Switch Brief vs competing-offers proof on Tier 1 before cloning to lower tiers.

thresholds.action: Scale the tier and clone winning angles downward
Keep running; tighten personalization on {{competitor}} or {{finance_phrase}}
Test a subject or offer variant before cutting
Cut the tier and move volume to the next exclusive route
